name: LUXURY HONG KONG COUNTRY COW SHED
description:
Your bijoux getaway is a one story cottage in our fully private garden. 10 min bike + 30 min ferry ride to Central HK. A 15 min car free nature walk to taxi and bus. The 250 sq foot cowshed is just off hiking trails and is surrounded by nature. A rare find!
On your walk to the property you will pass farmer's fields, old style villages, cows and if you are lucky water buffalo. But you must walk or bike!
This is a way of life that is fast disappearing. Come and experience it for yourselves!
neighborhood_overview:
We are in the South Lantau foot hills, 20 min walk to Mui Wo beaches and ferry pier. 10 min by bike.
Our village is accessible by concrete village path suitable for bikes and tricycles.
All shops and transport 10 minutes from the house. Then a gorgeous cross harbour 30 min fast ferry ride lands you smack in Central HK!
Your cowshed is surrounded by banana plantations and farmer's fields. We are in a village but are completely private from the other houses.
In the neighbourhood we have temples, organic farms, waterfalls, rivers, hiking trails, mountains, sandy beaches, restaurants, a market, shops, sports centre, library, playgrounds, public basketball and tennis courts, bookstores, bars and cafes. Mui Wo Village and the rest of South Lantau is a wonderful place to explore.
The cowshed itself is right in the middle of amazing hiking paths. One minute from the door step is a beautiful rocky river to explore.
So lucky! Best of city and country in one!
host_about: I'm a (We are) fun loving neo-hippy(ies)  (that is what my partner Morgan says to write!).... We've lived all over the world and chose Hong Kong for a reason.  Come find out why!  We love to host and can point a traveler in any direction needed in Hong Kong and the entire Asia region!  Sharing is what it is all about.  We are film makers and teachers.  We do have busy lives so we combine just the right mix of meddling (so that you are comfortable) and staying out of your way (so you can be yourself).  Life motto?  Dunno: do it with passion.

name: Modern family-friendly suite in fishing village
description:
Our property is located in Tai O on Lantau Island, Hong Kong's largest and most unspoiled outlying island. Lantau is an off-track destination for those who look to escape to an alternative Hong Kong.

Tai O itself is a charming, traditional fishing village. We offer a comfortable home away from home so that guests can have time to explore and appreciate the crude beauty which is not possible to be found in downtown Hong Kong.
neighborhood_overview: Tai O villagers still lead a simple life. Unlike the urban fellow citizens, folks here are used to getting up very early and enjoy morning tea in the convivial atmosphere of local teahouses or “cha chaan teng”. Local restaurants serve the last call around 8 pm and are usually closed by 9 pm. Late night dining is only possible in a handful of small eateries. There are no chain supermarkets, convenient stores and fast food joints. Visitors will truly enjoy tranquility here though some conveniences have to be compromised. No vehicles are allowed beyond the parking area/ bus terminus/ taxi stand.
host_about:

"Being elegantly simple" is our attitude. Our company's mission is to help sustain Tai O's crude beauty by offering our guests a comfortable home from home so that they will have time to explore and appreciate this charming traditional fishing village.

Hong Kong brings out the best & worst in you... ^_^

host_about:
Founded by backpackers and soultrippers, The Mahjong is the result of years of pursuing a dream to establish a comfortable boutique hostel that offers cultural immersion in addition to a social exchange for travelers to meet and swap stories.

The Mahjong takes its name from a traditional game that dates back to late Qing dynasty when locals gathered together over a table of 144 game pieces to play and while away the days. Today, the game has evolved into a national pastime and is played everywhere – at home, in the park, even dedicated mahjong parlours around the city. There are various legends on how the game got its name – one being the Mahjong sparrow it was named after, for its petite yet agile body that resembled the game pieces.

neighborhood_overview:
Sai Ying Pun is an exciting, up-and-coming district on Hong Kong Island. The street is unique and has a lot of character. There are plenty of restaurants and supermarkets around, as well as a beautiful historical building dating back 1892, a quaint old brick house and a sports ground.

Life is easy here, with plenty of good retaurants (French, Italian, Thai, Japanese, Spanish, Cantonese noodles, etc), convenience stores, grocery shops, laundry shops, supermarkets and a wet market. An escalator has been installed a few years ago, making life even easier and the neighbourhood livelier. From the tramway, you walk uphill a bit and there are escalators transporting you all the way to the Mid-Levels, where there are banks, more laundry shops and restaurants.

The neighbourhood is an interesting mix of people: urbane types, young professionals, expats from different parts of the world, down-to-earth locals and laid-back, friendly elderly people.

Mong Kok has entire streets and street sections dedicated to the sale of goldfish, flowers, birds, sneakers, and kitchenware.

neighborhood_overview:
Sai Ying Pun is an area in Western District, in the northwestern part of Hong Kong Island, in Hong Kong. It is administratively part of Central and Western District.

In Chinese language (Cantonese dialect regarding the spoken version), Sai (西) means "west" and Ying Pun (營盤) means "camp", especially military camp. It was where the early British military (website hidden) Ying Pun is built on the steeply sloping lower slopes of Victoria Peak and also on the western reclamation. The areas of Shek Tong Tsui and Kennedy Town are located to the west, Sheung Wan and Tai Ping Shan are to the east, and Midlevels is higher on the hill to the south. Victoria Harbour is to the north.

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Sai Ying Pun is very well located and a short distance away (two MTR stops and about 7 minutes) from the hub of Central, the business district of Hong Kong.

In Sai Ying Pun itself there are many quaint restaurants, an awesome art gallery and other attractions. It is lovely to walk the streets to discover hidden treasures. There is a place that serves as well as educates it's customers on the finest beers, a beautiful memorial park in which to enjoy a lazy day, and temples to visit too.

Going further out of Sai Ying Pun, a great way to find out more about Hong Kong is to hop on a bus to visit one of many special places. You could also catch a ferry to Macau, which is classified as a different country to Hong Kong, although it is within a 45 minute ferry ride.
host_about:
Hello, I am a South African who grew up in beautiful Cape Town and lived for approximately 18 years in Johannesburg before moving overseas. I love the ocean, snorkeling, reading, dancing, singing and traveling. Oh, and of course, children, as that has been my life's work. However, I am open to all possibilities, as I believe we are limitless.

I love to laugh out loud, perhaps because of a thought that has made me happy, to contemplate on this world and the part I play in it, to feel salty ocean water on my legs, to appreciate life's little nuances, have immense gratitude for the life I have, and to dance with abandon. 

I have been to London, UK, once, and loved it. Mauritius twice (late 90's and early 2000's) - love the place, the people, the beauty of the island. I traveled to Australia (Perth) for 5 days in 2013 (met up with my dear Aunt and traveled to New Norcia), and had my first Airbnb experience (it was lovely, with friendly hosts), and also visited New Zealand (Auckland - 2013), where my brother and his wife and family live (loved my time with them and visited Wellington for a few days too, which was great). I have also spent time in Muni-ki-reti, India, at the Divine Life Society, twice (2011 and 2015), which was a wonderful experience.

I moved to Hong Kong at the end of September 2016, and find life here very interesting. Since moving over, I have visited Koh Samui, Thailand twice (October and December 2018), Hoi An in Vietnam (November 2018), Macau (many times), Melaka, Malaysia (April 2019), Phuket, Thailand (May 2019), Morocco (July 2019)  and of course have had many trips back home. I continue to look forward to other destinations.

I love to meet new people, listen to their stories, and enjoy interesting conversations. I also enjoy quiet time. As a yogi, I try and use all experiences to better my life, and try to learn through every interaction. Sometimes people click so well, that shared time is wonderful and seamless, and the connection lasts long after one has said goodbye. 

I love connecting with humanity, whether it be in the form of people or animals. I find nature incredibly uplifting, invigorating, and soul enhancing, always. 

I am friendly, easy going, love to soak in every minute of each day, and am grateful for the opportunities that come my way in life, in which ever way it presents itself.

What I try and keep uppermost in mind always is this: Be the change you want to see in the world; Think before you speak

Happy days to you :)

As with most guesthouses in Hong Kong, we are upstairs in a mixed-use apartment block. There's a security guard in the main building lobby & an elevator going to our floor.

neighborhood_overview:
Location is very important. Our guesthouse is a short walk from the Temple Street night market, where you can get souvenirs. There's restaurants and "dai pai dong" (大牌檔 - Hong Kong-style open-air food stalls) nearby that are open until late.

A longer walk or short train or taxi ride can take you to the larger shopping malls in the area like Elements over Kowloon Station, as well as The One, K11 and Harbour City in Tsim Sha Tsui.

Take a short ride on the bus, train or taxi to the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade and Star Ferry Pier to enjoy the day or night view of Hong Kong Island across the harbour.

Pokemon Go players might like to note that our place is right next to the Temple Street Gateway Pokemon Gym, which has been known to host Legendary Raid Battles.

name: Newly Modern Luxe Lofts 4 Rooms Apartment
description:
Luxe Living Meets Urban Splendor in the Heart of Hong Kong!

Embark on a captivating odyssey through architectural brilliance as Vicael's visionary Interior Designer unveils the timeless allure of weathered brick walls harmoniously entwined with contemporary design marvels. Brace yourself for more than just an apartment; this is a transformative voyage that seamlessly intertwines history and modernity in a symphony of opulent industrial elegance.

Apartment is 3-min walking distance to Metro!
neighborhood_overview:
Sham Shui Po is one of the densest and most vibrant neighbourhoods in Hong Kong. It has a diverse mix of migrants, working-class familie. Sham Shui Po has many lively street markets, electronics outlets, fabric stores, restaurants and food vendors. It is also famous as a red light district on Fuk Wa Street, and Golden Shopping Centre for bargain electronics and accessories.

For those who are looking for electronics and accessories, the Apliu Street market is well known in Hong Kong. The vendors in this open-air street market sells a wide variety of products at reasonable prices, allowing individuals to trade second hand goods here. Different shops sell a variety of goods including industrial electronics, analog and digital radio communications equipment, disco effects equipment, crockery, 1940s-era radios, LPs, torches, and audiophile hi-fi amplifiers in various stages of repair. The Hong Kong government promotes Apliu Street as Hong Kong's answer to Akihabara (in Japan).
host_about:
Hi there, I am a New York architect and interior designer, I moved to Hong Kong in summer 2017, and this incredible city has been my home ever since. 

I run my own businesses and travel regularly for my jobs and for leisure of course! Blessed with the proximity to other fantastic places nearby, I have been busy travelling extensively around Asia ever since I arrived in HK, including Tibet, Nepal, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Japan, Bali etc. 

In my spare time, I enjoy going on the many fantastic hikes in HK, sipping bubble tea and cold beer on the beach, yoga, jazz, good coffee and a good book.

When I travel abroad I always use Airbnb. For me, a clean, comfortable and safe place to stay is essential. This is exactly what I offer to any guests staying with me. I hope that my place will be a little home-away-from-home for you during your time in HK.

Looking forward to hearing from you!

Vic

記得最激一次,是大學跟四位同學從廣州徒步到內蒙古｡經歷70多日的艱苦路程,回憶畢身難忘｡每一次旅程,除了令人難忘的風景,跟當地人的交流互動,都是每一次旅行都獨一無二的重要原素｡所以我希望透過開辦民宿旅館,認識世界各地不同的客人,希望我可以代表香港,歡迎每一位來到我們家的客人｡讓大家感受香港人這個城市的人情味和好客之道｡

neighborhood_overview:
Location is very important. Downstairs our guesthouse is the Temple Street night market, where you can get souvenirs. There's restaurants and "dai pai dong" (大牌檔 - Hong Kong-style open-air food stalls) nearby that are open until late.

A longer walk or short train or taxi ride can take you to the larger shopping malls in the area like Elements over Kowloon Station, as well as The One, K11 and Harbour City in Tsim Sha Tsui.

Take a short ride on the bus, train or taxi to the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade and Star Ferry Pier to enjoy the day or night view of Hong Kong Island across the harbour.

Pokemon Go players might like to note that our place is right next to the Temple Street Gateway Pokemon Gym, which has been known to host Legendary Raid Battles.

neighborhood_overview:
Location is important. Our guesthouse is right next to Jordan MTR metro station, so it's easy to get from here to other parts of the city. Our rooms are facing away from the main road, making it much quieter - especially important when you want a good night's rest.

We are a short walk from the Temple Street night market, where you can get souvenirs. There're restaurants and "dai pai dong" (大牌檔 - Hong Kong style open fair food stall) nearby that are open until late.

A longer walk or short train or taxi ride will take you to the larger shopping malls in the area like Elements over Kowloon Station, as well as The One, K11 and Harbour City in Tsim Sha Tsui.

Take a short ride on the bus, train, or taxi to the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade and Star Ferry Pier to enjoy the day or night view of Hong Kong Island across the harbour.

Due to its distance from major commercial cores and longtime inaccessibility by train, town development was less vigorous than in other parts of urban Hong Kong. neighborhood_overview:
Kennedy Town is at the western end of Sai Wan on Hong Kong Island in Hong Kong. It was named after Arthur Edward Kennedy, the 7th Governor of Hong Kong from 1872 to 1877. Administratively, it is part of Central and Western District.
Due to its distance from major commercial cores and longtime inaccessibility by train, town development was less vigorous than in other parts of urban Hong Kong. But since the MTR was extended to the area in 2014, it is rapidly gentrifying, with many older businesses, such as vehicle repair workshops and cha chaan tengs, making way for new luxury developments, as well as high end bars and restaurants.

The main village is five minute walk from the apartment in which you can find a range of local, western or Asian ocean view restaurants. There are bars where you will often find the local residents sipping a beer strumming a guitar. Candela, The Waterfront and Blue Goose are all firm favourites. You won’t find better local food than at Sampan Restaurant, which serves authentic Chinese food.

description: Enjoy this downtown home with family and friends and go anywhere.
host_about:
Hello, I am Angel. I hope all of the guests have a nice stay in my guesthouse which is in the heart of Tsim Sha Tsui, you can come here with different methods:

1. Hong Kong airport to guest house by bus:

Take bus A21 in Airport. Get off in Tsim Sha Tsui named [Middle Road] bus stop, walks around 3-4 minutes to get there.

2. Metro Line from airport:

Airport >>>>Tsing Yi( Airport Express)
Interchange from Tsing Yi>>>>Nam Cheong (Tung Chung Line)
Interchange from Nam Cheong>>>>East Tsim Sha Tusi (West Rail Line)
Estimate journey time: 38 minutes

Exit East Tsim Sha Tusi station and walk to Tsim Sha Tusi Exit through subway. Takes around 2-3 minutes walk to the building.

3. Taxi: Take a taxi from the airport to guest house cost about $ 280.

4. Futian, Luohu Port or Port Directions: 

From the train station at Futian or Luohu, to Hung Hom Station, and then interchange to West Rail Line to East Tsim Sha Tsui station. 

Exit East Tsim Sha Tusi station and walk to Tsim Sha Tusi Exit D2 through subway. Takes around 2-3 minutes walk to the building.

name: [6A] Triple Room in Kowloon
description:
We're renting out rooms in our little guesthouse in Jordan, Hong Kong. It's right next to the famous Temple Street Gateway.

We're walking distance from the MTR subway station & the A22 airport bus stop is less than 100m away. This is a convenient place to stay & explore the city.

As with most guesthouses in Hong Kong, we are upstairs in a mixed-use apartment block. There's a security guard in the main building lobby & an elevator going to our floor.

Please message me for details.
neighborhood_overview:
Location is very important. Downstairs our guesthouse is the Temple Street night market, where you can get souvenirs. There's restaurants and "dai pai dong" (大牌檔 - Hong Kong-style open-air food stalls) nearby that are open until late.

A longer walk or short train or taxi ride can take you to the larger shopping malls in the area like Elements over Kowloon Station, as well as The One, K11 and Harbour City in Tsim Sha Tsui.

Take a short ride on the bus, train or taxi to the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade and Star Ferry Pier to enjoy the day or night view of Hong Kong Island across the harbour.

Pokemon Go players might like to note that our place is right next to the Temple Street Gateway Pokemon Gym, which has been known to host Legendary Raid Battles.

Pui O, located on the southern shoreline of Lantau Island, is an old fishing village with a picturesque setting between mountains and a long stretch of open beach. It has become a popular weekend and holiday destination for locals and visitors alike.

The main attraction of Pui O is its family-friendly beach, which spans approximately 700 meters from west to east. Visitors can enjoy various recreational activities and soak up the sun, providing a refreshing escape from the city's hustle and bustle.

Walking between the beach and the main village, you will pass through paddocks where Hong Kong's beloved feral buffalo, also known as cows, can often be spotted. Some of them even make their way to the beach. Along the South Lantau Island Road that cuts through the village, there are a few restaurants to satisfy your hunger.

However, it’s much more than just a shopper’s paradise. Venture beyond the multitude of malls and discover an alluring enclave that’s brimming with character, Hong Kong Island’s largest public park and a rich history tied to its past as a former fishing village.

Named after the cove that it’s now built on top of, Causeway Bay’s erstwhile coastline is today marked by Tung Lo Wan Road, while landmarks including a 19th century Tin Hau temple dedicated to the Goddess of the Sea, the Noon Day Gun and a bronze statue of British monarch Queen Victoria recall the territory’s Chinese and British influences.
